Use N–mm–MPa units.
Assume Euler–Bernoulli beam theory with small deflection and linear elastic behavior.
Use a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Use structural steel with E = 200000 MPa.
Use constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
Apply a downward point load P = 2000 N at the free end.
Take the free-end rotation to be zero because no external couple is applied at the free end.
Use the constant moment M = P L over the full span for the deflection calculation.
Compute the slope at the free end as 0 rad.
Compute the vertical deflection at the free end as delta = (P L^3) / (2 E I).
Substitute P = 2000 N, L = 1800 mm, E = 200000 MPa, and I = 1200000 mm^4 to obtain delta = 24.3 mm.
Report the slope as 0 rad and the deflection as 24.3 mm.
